subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm planning a seated koala model, about 0.7 m tall, hugging a branch with leaves in one hand, positioned so its base sits at y=0.

The branch should sit horizontally beneath the koala, with the arms wrapping around a diagonal section held near the chest, so the piece reads as "hugging" while the koala rests on top.

I'll simplify this: koala seated on the ground with a tree branch standing up beside it, tilted slightly, arms wrapped around the branch and leaves held near the mouth. That reads clearly as "koala hugging a branch" without needing complex geometry for forks or diagonal limbs.

Now I'm planning the actual build structure — joint hierarchy for hips, spine, neck, and head, plus the builder functions I'll use (joints, chains, parts, sweeps for the branch) to keep the code compact at around 250-300 lines while avoiding fragile APIs.

For the eyes, I'm working out how to give the koala a drowsy, half-closed look using a brown sphere for the eye and a fur-colored hemisphere cap positioned over the top portion to act as an eyelid.

I'll simplify by skipping the hemisphere approach and just using the `dir`/`axis:"z"` part option to orient eyes, nose, and ears toward the facing direction, which seems like the lower-risk path.

For ears I'm going with flattened scaled spheres (grey outer, cream inner cap) and planning to use countershade for the body's ash-fur coloring instead of fussing with fur textures. I'm narrowing down my imports to just the functions I'll actually use: createBuilder, catmull, bezier, countershade, mottle, and rng.

For the leaves I'm shaping a lanceolate eucalyptus outline and extruding it along stem positions, placing sprigs near the hand using local x/y directions from each extrusion point rather than full frame tracking. For the branch, I'm sweeping a catmull curve from the ground upward with tapering radius, then figuring out where to position it relative to the koala's shoulder and arm reach so the arms can plausibly wrap around it.

I'm working out the koala's pose: left arm (positive X) hugging the branch via inverse kinematics from shoulder to a grasp point on the branch surface, while the right arm (negative X) holds leaves near the mouth. I'm calculating the specific shoulder, hand, and target coordinates needed for the limb IK to look natural.

For the hind legs I'm sketching bulky thigh spheres and forward-facing feet near the ground, then adding claw spikes using the spike primitive with a base point, direction, length, and radius, checking how color options get passed into that call.

Now I'm placing the head sphere near the neck joint, sizing the torso and cream chest patches with scaled spheres, and sketching out the spine joint chain from hips to neck to set up the rig.

For limbs I'm deciding to use chains with explicit joint names so each path point (hip/knee/ankle, shoulder/elbow/wrist) gets its own joint, adding a tip joint when I give one extra name, parented off the chest joint.

No tail needed since koalas have only a tiny stub. For coloring, I'm picking a grey/cream palette for the coat, dark nose and eyes, grey-green leaf tones for accessories, and planning to paint the body using a mottled grey texture rather than countershading, since that reads better as koala fur. Fine fur detail cards might be skippable for now.

For ear placement I'm figuring out the local coordinate words relative to the head joint — using signed "left" and "up" offsets so each side mirrors correctly, and I need to double check how the head's orientation inherits from the chest joint so the ears end up positioned naturally rather than skewed.

Since bone orientation conventions get confusing with the up/forward/back axis rules, I'm deciding to just rely on the named directional words (left, right, up, forward) consistently for every part placement rather than mixing in raw axis vectors, since those words stay correct regardless of bone roll. For the eyes and nose I'm placing them using head.local offsets with forward distance and vertical offset to position them on the face, sizing the nose as a scaled sphere to get that distinct koala snout shape.

Now I'm working out the ears: positioning them at head.local offsets near the top sides of the head, and considering how scaling the sphere flat along one axis will orient the disc shape -- thinking through whether that flattening should face forward or sideways to match how koala ears actually stick out from the head.

For the eye position, I'm placing it on the face front using local head coordinates with a slight forward offset so it sits embedded in the head sphere. For the eyelid, I'm using an upper hemisphere dome slightly larger than the eye radius, positioned at the same center so it covers the top portion while leaving the lower half of the eye visible, giving a drowsy look.

Now I'm setting up the nose as a scaled sphere positioned below and forward on the head.

For the mouth, I'm placing a sprig of leaves held by the hand near the mouth, mid-munch. I'm building a stem curve from the wrist to a point near the mouth, then generating leaf shapes extruded from a lanceolate outline along the stem, orienting each leaf's width and length axes to point outward and upward at a few points along the stem.

Positioning leaves along the stem...

I'll go with 5 leaves and use a sweep for the stem with a small radius and twig color, then sweep the branch with a tapered radius using bark colors and a grain texture for bark-like variation. For the branch bone attachment, I'll pick whichever joint is closest to the sweep's starting point, though it won't matter much visually for a static branch.

Checking that the branch stays fixed relative to the hips rigidly, I confirm it works since it's tied to the root. I think about whether the branch could clip into the koala's body — comparing the torso radius against the branch's position and radius, they seem to nearly touch, which works for a hugging pose. I then work out target positions for the left hand gripping the branch near the shoulder, checking distances fall within the arm's segment lengths.

Now I'm sketching out the arm sweep geometry with tapered radii for fur, placing the thighs and feet for a seated pose, and adding small claw spikes at the front of each foot and on the hands. I'm also setting up joint bones for the torso and hips, and starting to define a countershading color for the belly fur.

I'm thinking through the rig: hips and chest as spine joints, head joint for head parts, and chain roles for the arms, with the torso's cream chest sphere handled separately from the countershading. Now I'm starting to write the actual builder code, importing the geometry and shading utilities needed to construct the koala model.

Setting up colors and joints...

I'm defining the hip, chest, and head joints with their positions and parent hierarchy, letting unspecified joints inherit their parent's orientation. Then I'm building the torso as a scaled sphere attached near the hips, checking that it overlaps properly with the head geometry to avoid a visible neck gap.

I'm placing the chest accent sphere, thighs, and feet as scaled spheres with appropriate colors and bone attachments, then adding small claw spikes on the feet positioned and angled to sit at the front edge of each foot sphere.

Next I'm positioning the head sphere at the head joint, then building the ears as flattened disc shapes on either side of the head so they stick out laterally, computing their lateral offset relative to the head sphere's radius.

Now I'm checking the cream ear lining placement, sizing it smaller than the grey ear disc and offsetting it slightly outward so it sits like a rim on top of each ear, confirming the "left" axis convention maps to +X for the model's left side before moving on to building the eyes.

For the eyes I'm placing small spheres forward on the head so they protrude slightly past the surface for a stylized look, then adding a hemisphere-dome eyelid over the top half of each eye using the coat material, leaving the bottom open since it won't be visible from normal viewing angles. Now I'm moving on to adding eye highlights.

I'm positioning the nose as a slightly flattened sphere offset downward and forward on the head to create the bulging koala snout, and skipping a mouth detail for simplicity. For the left arm I'm defining shoulder and hand anchor points, computing a limb chain between them with a downward elbow bend direction for a branch-hugging pose, checking the reach distance stays within the joint limit, then building the arm chain with named shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints under the chest parent.

I'm sweeping a tapered tube along the arm chain for the limb shape, adding a hand sphere at the wrist tip with slight scaling, and attaching three small claw spikes angled forward and down from the hand surface. Now I'm setting up the mirrored right arm with shoulder and hand target points for a leaf-holding pose near the mouth.

I'm plotting a curved stem path from the wrist up toward the face using a catmull spline, then placing outward-facing leaf shapes along several points on that stem to form the munching leaves prop.

Typing the leaf outline array and sweeping the twig with a thin bevel, then building the branch path with a catmull curve and bark grain texture, checking that the hand position hugs the branch radius and doesn't collide with the torso surface.

I'm sanity-checking proportions — branch height versus koala height, hip joint placement, and making sure claws, thighs, and feet are properly set up on the limbs before finalizing imports and the metadata export for the build function.
